title: JumpCloud MFA, user and group changes
volume: None on a normal day for MFA. User creation by API comes with HR or SCIM sync, and group changes with onboarding, a few a day where admins manage groups by hand.
mdr_note: These detections are yours to work. Sophos MDR doesn't work custom detections, and a case your own case rule opens from them is Managed By Self.
author: Aaronjacobs000
summary: Three custom detection rules for JumpCloud, on the CloudAudit records the library's JumpCloud parsers write from Directory Insights. They make a detection when an admin turns off a user's MFA, a user is created with an API key, or a user group's membership changes. Each rule matches sensor type JumpCloud Directory Insights only.
notes:
Setup:
- Add the library's JumpCloud parsers and the example bridge in bridges/jumpcloud-directory-insights, and run the bridge with a read-only admin API key, as the parser entry says. Then run the check-your-data search to see events arrive.

How it works:
- The parsers write the Directory Insights event type, such as user_update, as the event name, the admin who made the change as the user, and the first three changed fields as request parameters, each as old to new.
- The MFA rule takes enable_user_portal_multifactor or totp_enabled going from true to false in one update.
- The API key rule takes users created with auth_method api-key, which the parsers keep in additional_event_data.

Tuning:
- If an HR or SCIM sync creates users with an API key, leave its admin out of that rule in the query itself, such as and user_name != 'hr-sync@example.com'. A suppression rule would hide Sophos's detections for that account as well.

Testing:
- In a lab tenant on 2026-11-23, each query returned exactly the sample lines tests.json lists in Data Lake Search, and the rules run offline on the same 3 records agreed. The samples went in with their dates moved to the day before the test, so they fell inside the search's time range.
- As live rules there, each one fired on exactly its sample lines within about a minute. The lines went in 22 minutes after the rules were made, and every rule fired on the first send.
- No Sophos detector made a detection on the lines these rules take. Sophos's sign-in analytics flagged only sample sign-ins on Auth, as an unseen user, address or application.
- The events went in through bridges/jumpcloud-directory-insights, run once on the lab machine against a local mock of the JumpCloud Directory Insights API that served the sample events, and posted to HTTP Ingest as gzipped NDJSON, the way the bridge's README says.

Known gaps:
- The bridge polls, so detections arrive up to one poll interval after the event.
- The parsers keep the first three changed fields of an update, so an MFA change made with many other changes in one save can be missed.
